problems.symptom: Scene loads with null references or loses exported node assignments after a text edit.
problems.cause: A broad .tscn replacement deleted or overwrote node_paths/reference metadata.
problems.solution: Revert the structural damage, perform a surgical edit, then run structural/scene-load validation.
problems.prevention: Use scene-safety; never rewrite unrelated node blocks for a small property change.

problems.symptom: Extreme G spike or chassis impact at curbs while suspension telemetry does not explain the hit.
problems.cause: A downward wheel RayCast starts below the obstacle top, so suspension probing misses the curb while the chassis collider hits it.
problems.solution: Verify curb geometry, chassis ground clearance and wheel RayCast origin/target before changing spring or damping values.
problems.prevention: Treat geometry and probe reach as first-class diagnostic inputs for curb-only impacts.

problems.symptom: The same bug receives multiple speculative patches without new evidence.
problems.cause: Attempt budget and diagnostic mode were not enforced.
problems.solution: Stop implementation, query common problems, inspect evidence/history, define a falsifiable hypothesis and run one diagnostic experiment.
problems.prevention: Second equivalent failure triggers problem lookup and diagnostic mode before another implementation attempt.

problems.symptom: Agent bootstrap routes to a skill path that does not exist.
problems.cause: Routing instructions and skill files drifted independently.
problems.solution: Use the central skill registry and run agentdb validate after registry/skill changes.
problems.prevention: Registry is the discoverable source for skill paths; validation must pass before an agent-system increment is accepted.
problems.source_ref: Observed in current Formula-90 bootstrap before this POC

problems.symptom: AgentDB commands fail even though the release binary exists; direct access reports unable to open database file and the Cargo fallback fails on target/release/.cargo-lock with Access denied.
problems.cause: The execution identity can read .agents but cannot write .agents/data/agents.db or its SQLite WAL/journal files, so the binary probe rejects a valid release binary and the resolver attempts an unnecessary build in a protected target directory.
problems.solution: Stop feature work, run the existing release binary and preflight in an execution context with write access to the configured database, or repair the ACL for the actual execution identity; then run stats, validate, health and smoke checks.
problems.prevention: Treat AgentDB access as a hard prerequisite. Do not rebuild blindly, recreate the database, interpret an unexecuted problem lookup as no known problem, or proceed with vehicle/physics/gameplay changes while AgentDB is unavailable.

problems.symptom: A Formula-90 .ps1 appears not to run from Explorer or PowerShell reports Get-Content Access denied for a vehicle manifest or GLB even though the containing folder looks accessible.
problems.cause: Explorer may register Microsoft.PowerShellScript.1/Open to a text editor and have no RunWithPowerShell verb, so opening a .ps1 is not execution. Independently, protected per-file ACLs can prevent child assets from inheriting permissions granted to their parent folder.
problems.solution: Check the registered .ps1 shell verbs and invoke the script explicitly with powershell.exe -NoProfile -File. Check Get-ExecutionPolicy -List separately. For a verified protected vehicle-asset tree, elevate only for that exact folder: take ownership, enable inheritance, grant the interactive user (OI)(CI) Modify recursively, verify every file opens for read, then run the script smoke without Bypass.
problems.prevention: Do not rely on the Explorer Open/Open with association for project scripts; provide a project-local launcher if double-click execution is required. Keep generated runtime asset trees inheriting the project ACL and validate file reads before interpreting hashes or manifests as content mismatches.
